title: SSE legacy client shim + structured-chunk metadata for function-call idempotency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: provide a lightweight server-side compatibility shim that allows legacy SSE clients (which expect raw text/event-stream lines and ad-hoc JSON payloads) to interoperate with the new structured-chunk protocol used for function/tool calling and structured outputs. The shim must: 1) accept legacy event shapes and translate them into the structured chunk envelope used by modern clients; 2) attach per-chunk metadata that carries function-call routing, idempotency tokens, and resume offsets; 3) preserve our resumability and dedup guarantees when clients reconnect or resend overlapping ranges; 4) avoid adding significant latency or CPU overhead to the hot path.
design_notes: High-level approach: implement a translation layer in the HTTP event router that recognizes legacy SSE user agents or 'accept' headers and performs two things: (A) on emit: wrap legacy payloads into the canonical chunk envelope: {seq, offset, kind, meta, payload} where meta includes 'tool_call_id' (optional), 'idempotency_key' (server-assigned if absent), and 'compat_version':'legacy-1'; (B) on resume: accept both resume-token (new clients) and last-event-id style resume (legacy clients). Resume negotiation: server returns a unified ResumeToken that contains the authoritative offset and a small hash of the last 512 bytes to validate alignment. For legacy reconnects we accept Last-Event-ID and translate internally to the same ResumeToken flow.
framing_format:
Canonical chunk envelope (text representation for SSE):
- event: chunk
- id: <seq>
- data: <json-encoded-envelope>
Envelope fields:
- seq: integer (monotonic per-session)
- offset: token (opaque string across restarts)
- kind: 'output' | 'toolcall' | 'meta' | 'recovery'
- meta: { 'tool_call_id':string?, 'idempotency_key':string, 'compat_version':string }
- payload: string/structured-object
This text format allows forwarding to legacy clients while preserving structured metadata for server-side routing and de-duplication.
resume_and_recovery: Reconnect behavior: when a client reconnects it may present one of: (1) ResumeToken (new clients), (2) Last-Event-ID (legacy), (3) idempotency_key list (partial resend). Server will: validate presented identifier -> compute a reconcile plan -> stream a small 'recovery' chunk that describes the acknowledged offset and any bytes that will be replayed or skipped -> then stream the remaining canonical chunks. To prevent double-execution of tool calls, the server checks per-call idempotency_key before invoking downstream tools and will return a 'tool-executed' meta chunk if the tool call was previously completed.
idempotency_strategy:
- idempotency_key generation: clients may send one inside meta; if absent the shim assigns a stable server-side id based on session + seq range.
- dedupe table: lightweight in-memory LRU keyed by idempotency_key -> execution result pointer (or 'in-progress').
- idempotent replies: when a tool call replay is detected, the server returns the original tool result chunk (with 'replay':true) instead of re-invoking the tool.
- garbage collection: entries older than 24 hours or when session is closed are evicted.
acceptance_criteria: Legacy SSE clients receive properly wrapped canonical chunks without breaking existing parsers (integration test against node-sse-client).
Reconnect flows using Last-Event-ID correctly map to resume offsets and no duplicate tool invocations observed in 1000 simulated reconnects.
Per-call idempotency keys prevent duplicate tool invocations under concurrent reconnects and partial resends.
End-to-end latency increase attributable to shim < 2ms p50 on our bench for typical payload sizes.
Unit/integration tests cover envelope translation, resume negotiation, and dedupe behavior.
updates: 2026-01-12 - Asha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem of INC-2026-01 (partial duplicate tool calls during reconnect).
2026-01-18 - Diego Morales: Spike complete; implemented experimental translator in dev router branch. Observed 1.8ms median overhead for 1KB payloads.

comments: Diego Morales (2026-01-20): Proposal adds a server-assigned idempotency_key when client doesn't provide one. Need to confirm KMS/HSM constraints for persistent dedupe table for Private installs.
Ritu Sharma (2026-01-24): Design looks good. Suggest we include a 'compat_version' value so future shim changes remain discoverable by clients.
Marcus Bae (2026-02-02): Align recovery chunk format with runtime-1.21 ResumeToken shape; I'll add a protobuf spec for the token so console and SDKs can parse deterministically.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: shim could leak internal metadata to legacy clients. Mitigation: always place internal fields under 'meta' and strip when sending to clients that signal absent structured-support; add unit tests to assert no internal headers pass through.

Risk: dedupe table memory growth under high throughput. Mitigation: LRU eviction + sampling-based exponential backoff for very large sessions; explore storing long-lived entries in redis for Dedicated/Private customers.

Risk: race between resume validation and tool execution leading to rare duplicates. Mitigation: conservative 'in-progress' locks keyed by idempotency_key; make tool invocations transactional where possible.
